record.paper_title: Where First-Order and Monadic Second-Order Logic Coincide
record.context_brief: FO versus MSO on induced-subgraph-closed graph classes
record.original_question: Which graph classes C that are closed under taking induced subgraphs have the property that first-order logic and monadic second-order logic define the same graph properties when formulas are interpreted only on graphs in C?

evidence.quote: Indeed, it is an open problem for which classes C of graphs closed under taking induced subgraphs FO ≡C MSO holds.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let FO denote first-order logic on the language of (finite simple undirected) graphs with a single binary edge relation, and let MSO denote monadic second-order logic on the same language (i.e., FO extended by quantification over sets of vertices). For a class C of finite graphs and two sentences φ, ψ, write φ ≡_C ψ if φ and ψ are satisfied by exactly the same graphs in C, and write FO ≡_C MSO if for every MSO sentence φ there exists an FO sentence ψ with φ ≡_C ψ.

Problem: Characterize precisely those classes C of finite graphs that are closed under taking induced subgraphs (i.e., if G ∈ C and H is an induced subgraph of G then H ∈ C) for which FO ≡_C MSO holds.
artifact.category_tag: finite model theory on graph classes
artifact.status_search_result: No characterization of induced-subgraph-closed graph classes on which FO and MSO are equally expressive appears in the literature. Known results give equivalence on restricted classes (e.g., bounded tree-depth, where every MSO sentence is FO-equivalent), and recent work on transductions characterizes related but distinct phenomena (FO-transductions of bounded-treewidth classes, etc.). The general classification problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: On first-order transductions of classes of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies FO-transductions and related characterizations of graph classes; no general FO≡MSO characterization for induced-subgraph-closed classes is given.
status_evidence.claim: Related characterizations are known but not a full answer to the FO≡MSO question on induced-subgraph-closed classes.

status_evidence.title: Understanding Some Graph Parameters by Infinite Model Theory
status_evidence.snippet: On classes of bounded tree-depth, every MSO sentence is equivalent to an FO sentence.
status_evidence.claim: FO=MSO is established for specific narrow classes (bounded tree-depth), but not characterized in general.
